top.title: Salah scores twice to create record as Egypt crush Malawi
top.description: Mohamed Salah celebrates after scoring for Egypt in a penalty shootout against Australia during the 2026 World Cup (Kevin C. Cox) Mohamed Salah scored twice as Egypt routed Malawi 5-0 in an Africa Cup of Nations qualifier on Friday to become the leading all-time scorer for his country with 70 goals. The 34-year-old former Liverpool star left it late in Cairo to overtake Hossam Hassan, scoring with a far-post header on 84 minutes and from a penalty five minutes into added time. Hassan was fired as Egypt coach last week and replacement Ali Maher made a perfect start with goals from Nasser Maher, Omar Marmoush and Mohamed Hany building a 3-0 lead by half-time. Egypt have seven points in Group B after three matches, three more than Angola, who host South Sudan on Saturday. Achraf Hakimi, favourite to win a second successive African Footballer of the Year award next month, also bagged a brace as Group A pacesetters Morocco crushed Niger 5-1 in Casablanca. Substitute Tolu Arokodaro scored twice within eight minutes as Nigeria beat Tanzania 3-1 in Uyo to get their campaign back on track. Tunisia suffered a shock home 2-0 loss to Libya and Kenya scored in the final minute to snatch a surprise 2-2 draw away to South Africa. Alhassan Yusuf put Nigeria ahead after just 103 seconds and Alphonce Msanga equalised on 32 minutes following a rare Tanzanian attack. Arokodaro, scorer of six goals in his last five matches for Ajax Amsterdam, came off the bench for the second half and quickly made an impact. His near-post back heel off a low cross put Nigeria ahead a second time after 52 minutes and as the match reached the hour mark, he struck again, with a close-range shot. An ultimately comfortable victory lifted the Super Eagles to six points after three rounds in Group L, one point behind Guinea-Bissau, who drew 1-1 with Madagascar on Thursday. - Nigeria boost - Although bottom of the table with just one point, Tanzania are guaranteed a place at the 2027 AFCON as co-hosts with Kenya and Uganda. That means Guinea-Bissau, Nigeria and Madagascar must fight for one place at the 24-nation tournament, the first to be staged in east Africa since Ethiopia were the 1976 hosts. Nigeria were in trouble after a 3-0 hammering in Guinea-Bissau two months ago, but now have a clear path to a tournament they have won three times. Away wins over Tanzania, on Tuesday, and Madagascar in March, and a home win over Guinea-Bissau, also in March, will assure qualification. Tunisia are in Group H, which includes co-hosts and automatic qualifiers Uganda, and their record of reaching every AFCON tournament since 1994 is in peril. A 2-0 defeat at home to neighbours Libya leaves them bottom of the table with just two points, and a venue switch two months ago means their remaining three fixtures are all away. top.title: Haslem Sets The Tone For Giannis And Bam After Rough Start
top.description: Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images The Miami Heat are sitting at 5-6, a record that makes no sense for a team that traded the world to get Giannis Antetokounmpo. The Greek Freak is putting up big numbers, but the losses keep piling up. That kind of pressure usually makes stars question their choices. Instead, Heat legend Udonis Haslem stepped in to set the record straight for his new teammate. This week, Antetokounmpo was addressed directly by Haslem, the vice president of basketball development. The 46-year-old veteran told the star that he cannot pick and choose when the hard times happen. According to HITC , Haslem said: “I told Giannis today: ‘Listen, you don’t get to pick and choose when the adversity hits. You just pick and choose how you respond.'” This message cuts through the noise and tells the team exactly what they need to hear right now. Adversity Hits Early or Late Haslem knows this league better than most, having spent 20 years in a Heat uniform. He explained that bad stretches come for everyone, just at different times. Some teams face trouble at the start, while others get hit in the middle or at the end. The Heat are dealing with it right now, and Haslem sees that as a blessing in disguise. He told Antetokounmpo that getting the pain out of the way early is the better option than saving it for the end of the season. The advice is simple but hard to follow. You cannot change the schedule or the opponents, but you can control your reaction. Haslem noted that if a player gets to choose, they should choose to face the hard stuff now. This approach forces the team to grow faster instead of waiting for a crisis later. Bam Must Play His Own Game While Giannis gets advice on mindset, center Bam Adebayo gets a reality check on his style. Haslem told Adebayo to stop trying to be someone else. The veteran captain made it clear that Adebayo has the talent to score 30 points a night, but he needs to do it his way. According to HITC, Haslem said: “You’re an effort and energy guy, that has All Star talent. You’re not Joel Embiid.” Haslem pointed out that Embiid can score from a kneeling position, but Adebayo’s path to those numbers requires constant motion and intensity. The goal is not to copy a different player’s moves but to use his own unique strengths to dominate. Before retiring, a man who previously shared a locker room with Adebayo made these comments. Haslem has watched Bam grow into a leader and knows exactly what he brings to the floor. The Heat need both stars to buy into these roles to fix their defensive rating, which currently sits as the fifth-worst in the league. The team faces a long road to fix their defense, but the leadership is finally speaking up.

top.title: France hold on for thrilling Nations Championship win over South Africa
top.description: France beat South Africa for only the second time in their last 11 Tests dating back to 2009 (FRANCK FIFE) France pulled off a stunning and nervy 21-19 victory over world champions South Africa in the Nations Championship on Friday. A brilliant first-half display and gutsy second-half showing amid a flood of cards handed Les Bleus only their second win over the Springboks in their last 11 Tests. Captain Antoine Dupont was named man of the match in a pulsating encounter that contrasted the running invention of the French with South Africa's bludgeoning force. And in the end, the only difference was a missed conversion by Springboks replacement fly-half Manie Libbok. France, though, were almost undone by wayward kicking, especially from half-back Maxime Lucu. The hosts' backs sparkled in the first half with wings Aaron Grandidier-Nkanang and Louis Bielle-Biarrey, and full-back Theo Attissogbe scoring a try each in a scintillating first half. But South Africa's brute force and forward power kept them in touch, scoring two catch-and-drive tries. Tries from hookers Jan-Hendrik Wessels and Malcolm Marx, and a close-range effort from replacement scrum-half Cobus Reinach, helped them storm back from a 21-7 half-time deficit, but it was not enough. It was South Africa's first defeat in the tournament and hands the initiative to New Zealand in the southern hemisphere pool. France, though, ensured that they will maintain their lead in the northern hemisphere section ahead of next weekend's clash against Argentina, keeping them in pole position to reach the final at Twickenham in two weeks' time. - Electrifying - The build-up to the match had been peppered with mind games. Having been named on the team sheet at fly-half, Dupont played at scrum-half with Lucu outside him. And an hour before kick-off, South Africa coach Rassie Erasmus swapped his entire starting front row with the three players initially named on the bench. France blew two early chances to open the scoring as Lucu kicked for the corner instead of the posts. The first time he fluffed his lines and South Africa won a penalty at the subsequent scrum. And the second time, the Springboks stole the line-out. But things turned in France's favour on 13 minutes as Bok lock Lood de Jager saw yellow for a high tackle on Lucu. Grandidier-Nkanang made them pay after 15 phases of play by diving over in the corner, with Lucu converting. And before De Jager returned, Attissogbe pounced on a lucky ricochet off Kalvin Gourgue's head to score a second. South Africa hit back on the half-hour mark with a classic tactic. Their scrum won a penalty, which they kicked to the corner before mauling hooker Wessels over for the try. But France hit back immediately as hooker Peato Mauvaka, who was a last-minute replacement for Julien Marchand, broke from a ruck and Dupont sent in a delectable grubber for the electrifying Bielle-Biarrey to notch his 30th try in 29 Tests. top.title: Willis On IR: Dolphins Coach Shuts Down Any QB Debate For Now
top.description: Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images The Miami Dolphins made their move on Tuesday by placing starting quarterback Malik Willis on injured reserve. Placing starting quarterback Malik Willis on injured reserve comes after an MRI on Monday showed his core muscle injury had gotten worse. Coach Jeff Hafley confirmed the team’s stance on Wednesday, stating there will be no quarterback controversy while backup Kyle McCord takes over. The coaching staff wants Willis to rest so he can return healthy, but the immediate path forward belongs to McCord. Hafley explained that he watched Willis struggle to move during the loss to Detroit in Week 9. “You look back at Malik and you watch him in that last game and you could see it,” Hafley said Wednesday, according to WPBF . He noted that Willis was gritting through the pain but could not move like he did earlier in the year. The team signed Willis to a three-year, $67.5 million deal in March, yet his health remains the biggest question mark for the franchise. McCord Takes The Reins Kyle McCord is now the man under center for the upcoming matchup against the Indianapolis Colts. This summer, McCord was obtained by the Dolphins from the Green Bay Packers in exchange for a future sixth-round pick. He has not taken a regular-season snap for Miami yet, but he is ready to compete. “I pride myself on just being the ultimate competitor out there on the field,” McCord said Wednesday, according to Sports Illustrated . He believes his speed in processing information and accuracy will help him succeed in his first NFL start. Hafley was clear that he sees no debate about who starts if Willis does not return soon. “You guys will ask me,” Hafley said, “yes, he’ll be the starting quarterback if he returns.” The coach added that the team needs to get through the next four weeks to see how many games remain in the season. “I think you get through these four weeks, so it would leave four or five games left, and we’ll see,” Hafley said. This timeline will determine if the team can bring Willis back before the season ends. A Tough Road Ahead In his initial eight starts, Willis has thrown six touchdowns and six interceptions while completing 58.2% of passes for 1,396 yards. He showed the arm talent and mobility that brought him to Miami, but his decision-making has been inconsistent. The loss to the Lions on Sunday, Nov. 8, was ugly, with Willis throwing an interception and recording just 128 passing yards. His groin tightness during that game signaled the injury was becoming a major issue. The Dolphins face a difficult stretch without their planned franchise quarterback. They will play the Colts on Sunday, Nov. 15, at 1 p.m. ET at Lucas Oil Stadium.

top.title: Zach LaVine Wants Giannis, Heat Eye Free Agents After Slow Start
top.description: Credit: Sergio Estrada-Imagn Images The Miami Heat face a tough reality just three weeks into the 2026-27 season. They sit at 5-6 and need wins against weak teams to stay near .500. Sacramento Kings guard Zach LaVine reportedly wants to play alongside Giannis Antetokounmpo in Miami. The Heat look for immediate help to fix their roster holes. Heat insiders say the team is desperate for better perimeter depth. They have tried to fill gaps with mid-level exceptions, but the results are mixed. Adding a high-volume scorer like LaVine would change the offense. He is averaging 22.3 points per game this season. LaVine Could Fix the Backcourt LaVine is 31 years old and has only four postseason games in his career. He might be looking for a new challenge to boost his resume. According to Heavy.com , NBA insider Jake Fischer reported that Miami is a spot that LaVine would “like to go to.” The Heat cleared their roster to get Giannis, leaving them thin on the wings. They added Klay Thompson and Tim Hardaway Jr., but the depth is still shaky. Among league guards, LaVine previously ranked as one of the top scorers. His numbers have dipped, but his touch remains sharp. He played a career-low 25 games in 2023-24 due to injuries. His scoring ability next to Antetokounmpo would force defenses to choose between two threats. Giannis Is Staying Put While the Heat hunt for new pieces, the future of their star remains uncertain. ESPN front office insider Bobby Marks says Giannis will sign a new deal soon. “Giannis will extend with them either in January or sign a new deal this summer,” Marks said, according to BasketNews.com . He added, “So, it’s not like we’re putting, you know, he’s going to be looking at other things, right?” Giannis is in year two of his fully guaranteed three-year, $175 million max deal. He can choose to keep a player option worth $62.8 million for the 2027-28 campaign. Beginning Jan. 6, a four-year, $275 million extension becomes available for him to sign. If he waits until summer 2027, he could get a five-year deal worth $357 million. The Heat have secured their cornerstone, but the supporting cast needs work. Other Options on the Table The Heat are not just looking at LaVine. They are also considering veteran free agents Kevin Porter Jr. and Gabe Vincent. Porter Jr. offers versatility and could play multiple positions off the bench. Vincent has history with the team and helped them reach the NBA Finals in 2020 and 2023. The Heat have a game against the Cavaliers on Friday. They need to win that matchup to build momentum. The team is 5-2 in their last seven games, but they beat weak opponents.

top.title: Davion Mitchell Is The One Heat Player They Can’t Lose
top.description: Credit: David Kirouac-Imagn Images The Miami Heat cannot afford to lose Davion Mitchell. He has become the engine that keeps this team moving forward. Without his steady hand and elite defense, the roster falls apart fast. The stats prove he is the most vital piece on the court right now. Mitchell is playing as much as much as Bam or Giannis on the team. He has averaged 35.8 minutes per game, which tops the entire roster. His scoring numbers are strong too, with 16.5 points and 8 assists per contest. According to Sports Illustrated , he shoots 49.6 percent from the field and 40.3 percent from three-point range. Those splits are rare and show he does not force bad shots. The Bench Struggles Are Real While Mitchell thrives, Tim Hardaway Jr. is stuck in a deep hole. Hardaway started the season with high hopes but has failed to deliver. He is scoring only 4.3 points per game and shooting under 30 percent from the floor. His defense has been a major problem as well. Coach Erik Spoelstra has had to cut his minutes down to almost nothing. After a game against Utah where Hardaway sat out completely, Spoelstra spoke about the need for change. He said, “I get it for Timmy…sometimes you have to make a change.” The team simply cannot play him if he cannot guard or score. Ryan Conwell has taken his spot because he plays with more energy. Clutch Time Is The Test Mitchell shines when the clock runs low and the pressure is high. The Heat as a team struggles in these late-game moments. They shoot just 32.1 percent with under four seconds left on the clock. This is the fifth-worst mark in the league. When the clock gets tight, their three-point percentage drops to a terrible 22.6 percent. Mitchell flips that script with his own shot. He has a 40 percent field goal percentage in late shot clock situations. He is tied for sixth in the league for three-point shooting in those same moments. Yahoo Sports notes that the logic of playing only who is in front of you is faulty, yet Mitchell proves his worth every night. The Heat have won five of their last seven games, but they still need to face tougher foes. The next five opponents include the Cleveland Cavaliers, Detroit Pistons, and Houston Rockets. At least three of these teams are among the elite in the NBA. The Heat must go at least 4-1 over this stretch to get on track. top.title: Nikki Hiltz Tells Their Story of Becoming an Olympian After Coming Out as Trans in “Kick”: ‘A Sports Epic’ (Exclusive)
top.description: Credit: Curren Sheldon NEED TO KNOW Olympic runner Nikki Hiltz tells their story of life as a trans nonbinary athlete in new documentary Kick , alongside fiancée and fellow track and field star Emma Gee “Obviously, it’s not gonna be perfect, but it’s so worth it to try and go for something and let the world surprise you with their support,” Hiltz tells PEOPLE Kick, directed by Julia Schwalb, is available to watch online from Nov. 12 through Nov. 29 Nikki Hiltz doesn’t shy away from telling their story. The Olympian and 11-time national champion, 32, has always been candid about competing in the sport they love as a trans nonbinary athlete. And now, in collaboration with filmmaker Julia Schwalb , Hiltz along with their fiancée and fellow track and field athlete Emma Gee are giving audiences a glimpse into their individual queer journeys and their shared dreams of winning an Olympic medal in the new documentary Kick . Prior to the film’s premiere at DOC NYC on Nov. 11, PEOPLE caught up with Hiltz and Gee, learning how they decided what to share on screen, what they hope audiences take away from the film and how the idea for Kick came to be. “Julia approached me and we got on a Zoom call,” says Hiltz. “One of the first questions she asked was, ‘Okay, if there were to be a film about you, what would you want it to be about?’ And I was like ‘Oh, well, I want a sports movie.’ I’m an athlete and I love a sports epic, you know? That’s sick. I also happen to be queer and nonbinary and that could be part of the film too, obviously, because it’s part of me.’” Nikki Hiltz after winning the women’s mile at the 2026 Prefontaine Classic Credit: Ali Gradischer The pitch for Kick came at the perfect time: when Hiltz was gearing up for the 2024 Olympic Trials, in the hopes of becoming a first-time Olympian. “I was like, ‘Well, I have this big thing coming up. I’m trying to make the Olympics next year. Do you want to film that?’ ” Hiltz says they asked Schwalb. “So it kind of just took off from there.” Three years earlier, Hiltz had hoped to make Team USA for the Tokyo Olympics but finished last in the 1500-meter women’s final, ending their shot. Heading into the 2024 Trials with Hiltz and a camera crew, Gee had some doubts. “There was definitely some apprehension,” she tells PEOPLE. “We had been through the 2021 Olympic Trials together and it was super emotional...During this second Olympic journey, I just wanted to make sure Nikki’s mental health was in a good place — that we were in a safe space to even share this story.” “But we ultimately decided, you know, we’re gonna be on this Olympic journey, whether it’s filmed or not,” she continues. “And I think that it could potentially do a lot of good and offer, you know, representation to not only queer people, but anyone who’s trying to achieve a big goal.” The good news? top.title: Chris Bell Injury Hits Dolphins Right Before Key Week
top.description: Credit: Rich Storry-Imagn Images Chris Bell The Miami Dolphins face a tough spot with rookie wide receiver Chris Bell likely missing Sunday’s game against the Indianapolis Colts. Head coach Jeff Hafley said Bell would probably be listed as doubtful due to a knee injury, per Sports Illustrated . This is a setback, but it is not the torn ACL that ended Bell’s college season last year. The pain came during a practice hit on Wednesday, which stopped him from working on Thursday and Friday. Bell’s season has been rough so far, even though he made the team out of training camp. He has played in all eight games but only caught 12 passes for 148 yards, according to Sports Illustrated. That average of 12.3 yards per catch shows some big plays, yet he has zero touchdowns. The rookie also failed to catch a single ball in three different games, including the loss to Detroit where he was targeted just once. Depth Chart Gets Thin The injury report hurts the Dolphins because they need more help for quarterback Kyle McCord. McCord steps in for the injured Malik Willis and needs reliable targets to feel comfortable. If Bell sits out, fifth-round rookie Kevin Coleman Jr. could see more time, per Yahoo Sports . The team already has Caleb Douglas and Malik Washington ahead of Bell in the rotation. Veteran Jalen Tolbert might return to the lineup if Jared Wayne stays out with his own quad issue. Other Key Absences Loom Bell is not the only player dealing with health problems this week. Center Aaron Brewer will miss the game because he is still in concussion protocol, Hafley confirmed. Andrew Meyer will start in his place at the center position. Will Kacmarek, the tight end, is expected to play after skipping practice earlier in the week. Cornerback Darrell Baker Jr. likely stays off the active roster after his first week back from the PUP list. The Dolphins and Colts both want to win, but the injuries make this a messy matchup. Rookie linebacker Trey Moore remains on injured reserve with a significant ankle injury from the preseason. Hafley said he was “hopeful” that Moore could return this season, though that looks like a 50-50 chance at best. The game kicks off at 1 p.m. ET on Sunday at Lucas Oil Stadium.

top.title: Andorra goalkeeper banned for 12 matches after Jesus de Miguel’s death following on-pitch collision
top.description: A 12-match ban has been handed to Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono following the death of Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel after an on-field collision between the pair. The Spanish soccer federation’s disciplinary committee imposed the suspension on Friday, 10 days after De Miguel died a day following his clash with Owono. The goalkeeper had received a red card following the incident, and the disciplinary committee said Owono used “excessive force” in the collision. The incident took place near the end of the match in Tenerife on 2 November. De Miguel was chasing a high ball in midfield when he was struck in the chest by Owono, who had rushed far outside his area. The 30-year-old suffered cardiac arrest following the collision. He died the next day. Owono issued a statement through his club expressing his remorse and offering his condolences to De Miguel’s family. Tributes have been paid to Jesus de Miguel following his death (Getty) “These are the most difficult days of my life,” Owono said. “I’m struggling to find the words and finding it very difficult to process anything that has happened. “I feel enormous pain at the loss of Jesus. I think of him, his family, and all the people who loved him. I know there will be many issues to address, and I will face whatever comes with the utmost respect. But right now, honestly, I can’t think of anything other than Jesus and the pain we are experiencing. Rest in peace, Jesus.” Spanish police opened an investigation into possible involuntary manslaughter. Under Spanish law, deaths from non-natural causes, including accidents, are subject to judicial investigation, though prosecutors have said that criminal proceedings are unlikely. On Thursday, Andorra coach Carles Manso said it will be up to Owono to decide when he feels ready to play again. “He is deeply affected by the situation,” Manso said. “We will give him the space to feel completely free to decide whether, and when, he might want to return.” Owono was not selected by Equatorial Guinea for their Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers during the ongoing international break following last week’s collision. Owono has been Equatorial Guinea’s first-choice goalkeeper since he was a teenager and competed with them at the last three Africa Cup of Nations finals.

nigeria.description: Portugal midfielder Bernardo Silva said Friday his team could cope with any extra pressure on them following Cristiano Ronaldo’s international retirement, ahead of their first match without the superstar forward. Jorge Jesus’s side host Denmark in Braga on Saturday in the Nations League, with a tribute planned for their all-time leading goalscorer. Real Madrid’s Silva, who inherits the captain’s armband from Ronaldo, admitted that the striker had been the main focus for much of the past two decades but backed the team to cope with the pressure in the 41-year-old’s absence. “Everyone knows the weight Cristiano carries. nigeria.description: By Favour Ulebor, Abuja The Federal Government has warned Nigerians, particularly those with pre-existing medical conditions, to exercise caution when travelling through Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, following the deaths of 16 Nigerians in the city this year. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs disclosed this in a travel advisory issued on Friday, stating that the deaths recorded by Nigeria’s Diplomatic Mission in Addis Ababa were reportedly linked to health complications associated with the city’s high altitude. The ministry explained that Addis Ababa is situated approximately 2,355 metres (7,726 feet) above sea level, where lower atmospheric pressure results in reduced oxygen availability. It noted that the conditions could pose increased health risks to travellers with certain underlying medical conditions, particularly cardiovascular and respiratory ailments. According to the advisory, although healthy individuals are generally able to adapt to reduced oxygen levels in high-altitude environments, people with certain pre-existing health conditions may experience complications. The Federal Government therefore advised Nigerians whose medical conditions could be worsened by high altitudes to seek appropriate medical advice before undertaking journeys involving transit through the Ethiopian capital. It also urged travellers with underlying medical conditions to consult medical professionals and obtain necessary guidance before embarking on their trips. The ministry, however, clarified that the advisory was not intended to discourage Nigerians from travelling to or transiting through Addis Ababa. Rather, it said the notice was aimed at ensuring that medically vulnerable travellers were adequately informed about the possible effects of high altitudes and took necessary precautions. nigeria.description: FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono was suspended for 12 matches by the Spanish football federation’s disciplinary committee on Friday after his challenge on Jesus de Miguel resulted in the death of the Tenerife striker last week. Equatorial Guinea international Owono was sent off in the second division clash on November 2 after racing into midfield and colliding with De Miguel while trying to clear an aerial ball. After the collision De Miguel, 30, was placed in intensive care in hospital and the Spanish forward died on November 3. “The assessment of the conduct under consideration in these proceedings must be based on the facts expressly recorded in the referee’s report, which states that the player was sent off for ‘violently striking an opponent in the chest with his leg, using excessive force, while the ball was in play’,” said the committee in a statement. “The tragic outcome of the incident, resulting in the death of Jesus de Miguel Alameda, is public knowledge. “In view of the nature of the conduct described and the accompanying circumstances… the maximum sanction, 12 matches of suspension, is justified.” Spanish police sources last week told AFP an investigation into what happened had been opened under judicial supervision. Owono said he was enduring the “hardest days of my life” after De Miguel’s death. “These are the hardest days of my life. I struggle to find the words and it is very difficult for me to process anything that has happened,” said Owono in a statement published by his club Andorra last week. “I feel immense pain over the loss of Jesus. I think of him, of his family, and of all the people who loved him. “I know there will be many issues to address, and I will face whatever comes with the utmost respect. nigeria.title: Lagos NDC meeting attack threatens democracy — APM candidate
nigeria.description: By Dapo Akinrefon The governorship candidate of the Action Peoples Movement (APM) in Lagos State, Prince Laja Adeoye, has condemned the attack on supporters of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) during their town hall meeting in Lagos, describing the incident as shameful and a threat to democracy. Adeoye said the disruption of the meeting at Classique Event Centre, Oregun, Ikeja, on Thursday, amounted to an infringement on the constitutional rights of citizens to assemble and freely express their political views. He warned that the use of thugs to disrupt opposition gatherings could heighten political tension ahead of the 2027 general elections. Adeoye said, “Nobody should be attacked for supporting a candidate of his or her choice. What happened in Lagos on Thursday was shameful and unacceptable in a democracy.” He described the incident as particularly disturbing, noting that Lagos had traditionally been regarded as a centre of political activities where parties and candidates could canvass for support. According to him, the attack was not merely against the NDC but also against the democratic process and Nigerians who believe in free and fair elections. The APM candidate urged the Lagos State Police Command to identify, arrest and prosecute those responsible for the incident, irrespective of their political affiliation or status. nigeria.title: Nasarawa pensioners begin enforcement of ₦4bn court order
nigeria.description: By Edwin Philip, Lafia A group of 601 retired civil servants in Nasarawa State has commenced enforcement of a court order directing the recovery of over ₦4 billion in outstanding gratuities and other entitlements owed them by the state government. The pensioners, under the aegis of the Concerned Group of Nasarawa State Pensioners, secured a consent judgment against the state government in 2020 over the alleged non-payment of their retirement benefits. Their spokespersons, Mr Simon Auna and Mallam Usman Adamu, disclosed the development while speaking with journalists in Lafia on Friday. The group said it subsequently obtained an order from the National Industrial Court, Makurdi, awarding 25 per cent post-judgment interest on the judgment sum, bringing the total amount being sought to over ₦4 billion. According to the pensioners, following the alleged failure of the state government to comply with the judgment, their lawyers approached the Senior District Court in Makurdi, presided over by Justice Ada Jack. The court subsequently directed six commercial banks to release funds belonging to the Nasarawa State Government, amounting to over ₦4 billion, for payment to the affected retirees. In a move to enforce the order, the pensioners’ legal team, accompanied by court bailiffs, visited some branches of one of the commercial banks in Makurdi, Benue State, where they removed some movable properties. Speaking on the development, counsel to the pensioners, Mrs Doofan Sefa-Aii, said the legal team would continue to operate within the law to ensure full recovery of the funds owed the retirees. Another counsel, Mr Awo Matthew, appealed to the Nasarawa State Government and the banks involved to allow the legal process to take its course, considering the hardship the pensioners had endured while pursuing payment of their entitlements. However, the Director of Corporate Services and Arbitration at the Nasarawa State Ministry of Justice, Mr Usman Aliyu, said the state government had taken all necessary legal steps, including filing a motion for a stay of execution of the court order. Meanwhile, Adamu, who is the group’s Lafia Local Government Chairman, and Auna, its Legal Adviser, described the court order as a significant breakthrough after years of seeking payment of their entitlements. They said the development had renewed their hope of recovering the outstanding benefits. The pensioners reaffirmed their determination to pursue their entitlements through lawful means until the matter was resolved. nigeria.title: Zulum offers soldiers N50,000 each, logistics for Borno deployment
nigeria.description: By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri Borno State Governor, Professor Babagana Umara Zulum, has announced a ₦50,000 welfare support for each soldier preparing for deployment to Maiwa and Koshebe communities in the state, alongside a pledge to provide operational logistics to strengthen security. Zulum gave the assurance on Friday during a visit to the headquarters of the 24 Task Force Brigade in Dikwa Local Government Area, where he met with the Brigade Commander, Brigadier General Aminu Gumel. The governor said the visit was aimed at exploring measures to improve security along the Maiduguri–Mafa–Dikwa–Ngala highway, a strategic economic corridor linking several communities in eastern Borno State. He noted that the highway was vital to trade, transportation and cross-border commercial activities, stressing that improved security would enable residents to travel safely, move agricultural produce and rebuild their livelihoods. “My visit is primarily aimed at exploring measures to strengthen security along the strategic economic corridor, which connects Maiduguri to several communities in eastern Borno and serves as a vital route for trade, transportation and cross-border commercial activities,” Zulum said. Addressing troops preparing for deployment to Maiwa and Koshebe, the governor pledged to provide operational logistics and sustained welfare support. He also announced a payment of ₦50,000 to each soldier preparing for the deployment to the two communities. Koshebe has previously suffered deadly attacks by suspected Boko Haram insurgents. On November 28, 2020, insurgents attacked rice farmers working in fields around the community, killing more than 100 people, many of whom were seasonal farm labourers from Sokoto State. Similarly, in November 2023, suspected insurgents attacked farmers harvesting rice in the Karkut and Koshebe areas of Mafa Local Government Area, killing at least 13 people, while others were reported missing. Zulum’s administration has continued to provide logistics and welfare assistance to security agencies as part of efforts to support military operations, improve security and facilitate the return of displaced residents to their communities. nigeria.title: COVID-19 loans must be repaid, NIRSAL MFB insists
nigeria.description: By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief NIRSAL Microfinance Bank (NMFB) has clarified that the COVID-19 Targeted Credit Facility (TCF) was an intervention loan, not a grant, stressing that beneficiaries are obligated to repay the funds. The bank said deductions from the accounts of beneficiaries who accessed the facility would continue until their outstanding loans were fully liquidated, in line with the Global Standing Instruction (GSI) mechanism. In a statement issued in Abuja at the weekend, the bank explained that the GSI framework allows financial institutions to recover outstanding loan obligations from eligible accounts linked to borrowers’ Bank Verification Numbers (BVNs), subject to applicable regulatory guidelines. The bank said the clarification became necessary to address concerns surrounding loan recoveries and reassure customers and members of the public of its commitment to transparency, accountability and responsible banking practices. It explained that the COVID-19 Targeted Credit Facility was introduced by the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) to support households and businesses affected by the economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic. According to the bank, all beneficiaries were required to accept electronic offer letters before disbursement, with the documents clearly outlining the terms and conditions of the facility, including repayment obligations and recovery mechanisms in cases of default. “Regarding the recovery process, the Bank operates within the applicable regulatory framework, including the Global Standing Instruction (GSI) mechanism approved by the Central Bank of Nigeria,” it stated. NIRSAL MFB, however, acknowledged concerns raised by some beneficiaries over the timing and amounts of deductions, outstanding loan balances and access to repayment information. The bank said it took the complaints seriously, noting that customers must have access to accurate information about their loan accounts. It stressed that the deductions were intended to settle outstanding contractual obligations, adding that beneficiaries who disputed deductions or identified discrepancies in their repayment records should contact the bank for individual account reconciliation. “Where any beneficiary has concerns about deductions made, discrepancies in repayment records or the status of an outstanding balance, such cases should be brought to the bank’s attention for individual account reconciliation and appropriate resolution,” it said. The bank assured that legitimate complaints would be investigated and that any discrepancies established during the reconciliation process would receive the necessary attention. It urged beneficiaries seeking clarification on their loan status, repayment history or outstanding obligations to contact the bank through its officially designated customer service channels. nigeria.title: Customs intercepts live sea turtle at Nigeria-Benin border
nigeria.description: By Efe Onodjae The Nigeria Customs Service (NCS), Seme Area Command, has intercepted a live endangered sea turtle allegedly being smuggled through a footpath linking Nigeria and the Republic of Benin. The Olive Ridley Sea Turtle, scientifically known as Lepidochelys olivacea, was intercepted during a routine patrol by Customs officers at about 10.30pm on Thursday, November 12, 2026. The command said the officers sighted a suspicious individual carrying a sack along the border route, but the suspect abandoned the bag and fled into a nearby bush upon noticing the patrol team. According to a statement by the command’s Public Relations Officer, Superintendent of Customs, John Tunde Ayagbalo, examination of the abandoned sack revealed the live sea turtle concealed inside. He said the animal was immediately secured and kept in safe custody before being handed over to relevant wildlife authorities for proper care, rehabilitation and eventual release into its natural habitat. The Acting Customs Area Controller, Seme Area Command, Deputy Comptroller Norman Olisah Alumanah, described the interception as a demonstration of the vigilance and professionalism of officers in tackling wildlife trafficking. Alumanah warned smugglers, poachers and their collaborators against using the nation’s borders as corridors for illegal wildlife trade, adding that the command had intensified patrols, surveillance and intelligence gathering across its area of responsibility. He also called on residents of border communities to provide credible intelligence to support the fight against wildlife trafficking. The Customs boss said the command would complement enforcement operations with stakeholder education and sensitisation on endangered species, their ecological importance and the legal implications of their unauthorised trade. Wildlife trafficking remains a major environmental crime, threatening biodiversity and the survival of endangered species through illegal exploitation for meat, eggs, shells, traditional medicine and the exotic pet trade. Nigeria is a signatory to the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES), which regulates international trade in endangered wildlife and plant species. The convention is domesticated in Nigeria through the Endangered Species (Control of International Trade and Traffic) Act, Cap E9, Laws of the Federation of Nigeria, 2004. nigeria.title: Ebola: All 62 contacts test negative after monitoring – NCDC
nigeria.description: By Chidinma Chukwu ABUJA — The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) has completed the 21-day monitoring of all 62 contacts linked to the imported case of Bundibugyo Virus Disease (BVD), a form of Ebola disease, confirmed in the Federal Capital Territory on October 20, 2026, with no secondary infections recorded. The Director-General of NCDC, Dr Jide Idris, disclosed this on Friday during a media briefing in Abuja, saying the last contact had been discharged from monitoring after testing negative for the virus. Idris said 13 of the 62 contacts reported fever or other non-specific symptoms during the monitoring period, but laboratory tests confirmed that none had contracted the disease. “The 21-day monitoring period for contacts linked to the index case has been completed, with the last contact discharged today. We are glad to announce that none of the contacts became ill with the disease, meaning no transmission from the index case. “A total of 62 contacts were identified, placed in quarantine and followed up by our public health teams. During the monitoring period, 13 contacts reported fever or other non-specific symptoms. All 13 were tested for Bundibugyo Virus Disease, and all tested negative,” he said. The index case was a 42-year-old Ugandan-born woman, who tested positive for the virus in Abuja on October 20. She was subsequently medically evacuated to Switzerland on October 26. Providing an update on her condition, Idris said the woman had recovered and been discharged from a hospital in Geneva. He also disclosed that seven additional suspected cases were reported and investigated in Adamawa, Rivers, Borno, Lagos and Ekiti states within the past three weeks. All seven cases tested negative for the virus. However, the NCDC chief cautioned against interpreting the completion of contact monitoring as a formal declaration that the outbreak was over. He explained that such a declaration would depend on established public health criteria and findings from continued surveillance. “It is important to note that the completion of contact monitoring does not, by itself, constitute a formal declaration that an outbreak is over. Such a determination must be based on the applicable public health criteria and the findings of ongoing surveillance. “Nigeria therefore remains vigilant, particularly given the continued occurrence of Ebola virus disease in the DRC,” he said. Idris assured Nigerians that disease surveillance and preparedness activities would continue, stressing that the agency remained committed to protecting residents and visitors. Looking ahead to the December festive season, he warned that increased travel, social interactions and large public gatherings could heighten the risk of disease transmission. nigeria.title: 2027: Tinubu, Atiku, Obi not there for Nigeria — Sule Lamido
nigeria.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Former Jigawa State Governor and PDP chieftain, Sule Lamido, has dismissed President Bola Tinubu, former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar and former Anambra State Governor, Peter Obi, as unsuitable options for Nigeria ahead of the 2027 general election. Lamido stated this during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Friday, where he was asked which of the three political figures could attract the Northern vote in the forthcoming presidential election. Giving his assessment, the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) chieftain said none of the three contenders was in a position to address Nigeria’s challenges. Peter Obi, Tinubu, Atiku — none of them is there for Nigeria.” The former Jigawa governor also declared his support for the PDP’s presidential candidate, Professor Sandy Onor, insisting that he remained committed to the opposition party and would not vote for Tinubu in 2027. nigeria.title: NSCDC disbands anti-vandalism outpost after Gombe incident
nigeria.description: By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe The Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), Gombe State Command, has ordered the immediate disbandment of its Anti-Vandalism Outpost following an incident involving its personnel and a truck driver in the state. The incident, which occurred on Thursday, November 12, 2026, reportedly followed a misunderstanding between personnel of the unit and a truck driver, resulting in the discharge of a firearm. The State Commandant, Commandant Muhammed Inuwa Usman, mni, also summoned all Officers-in-Charge (OCs) of the various formations and outposts to an emergency meeting on Friday to address the incident and reinforce professional standards among personnel. In a statement issued on Friday, the Command’s Public Relations Officer, Chief Superintendent of Corps Buhari Sa’ad, said the meeting was convened to address the incident and strengthen discipline and accountability within the command. During the meeting, Usman cautioned the officers against unprofessional conduct, indiscipline and actions capable of undermining the image of the Corps. He emphasised the need for personnel to remain professional, disciplined and civil, while respecting the fundamental human rights of members of the public in the discharge of their statutory responsibilities. The commandant also stressed that the use of firearms must strictly comply with established rules, operational procedures and applicable regulations, warning officers against taking the law into their own hands. As part of the disciplinary and administrative measures, he ordered the immediate disbandment of the Anti-Vandalism Outpost and directed all personnel attached to the unit to report to the State Command Headquarters without delay. Usman reiterated that the Corps would not condone indiscipline, abuse of authority or violations of citizens’ rights. He urged outpost commanders to strengthen supervision of their personnel and ensure strict adherence to the highest standards of professionalism and accountability. The commandant assured residents that the NSCDC remained committed to protecting lives and property, respecting human rights and maintaining peace and order in Gombe State. nigeria.title: England boss Tuchel eager to end Spain’s unbeaten run
nigeria.description: Thomas Tuchel believes England are ready to end Spain’s unbeaten record when they face the world and European champions in Madrid on Sunday. While victory offers not much more than the prospect of a more favourable Nations League quarter-final in March, it would be a landmark moment for England if they could end Spain’s run of 43 matches without defeat. “It (Spain) is a team that has forgotten how to lose, so of course it requires a top performance first of all, and if we can deliver this performance, it will give us a big boost,” said England manager Tuchel, whose side beat Croatia 2-1 at Wembley on Thursday. “I think we’re there, and I think we’re ready to win on Sunday,” the German added. “I know what it takes, and no one can ever guarantee it, but I think it’s the moment to check how far we are and to push our limit and proof of concept.” England lost the reverse fixture 3-2 at Wembley in September, but it might have been a different story had Harry Kane scored a penalty to put Tuchel’s team 3-1 up. “It’s important that we play with the same mindset that we played at home, and attack them and try to make it a physical game, and try to impose our strength.” England players have previously faced racist abuse in Spain, with Ashley Cole and Shaun Wright-Phillips targeted during a friendly in Madrid in 2004. Spain, meanwhile, must play their next home friendly with a reduced capacity as a punishment for supporters singing a discriminatory chant about Muslims during a fixture against Egypt in March. “We will never accept racism,” said Tuchel. “We will never be racist towards anyone.” He added: “I expect, of course, full support from the Spanish crowd for the Spanish team. But we will not expect anything. nigeria.title: Nigeria, EU seal €20m defence support deal
nigeria.description: By Kingsley Omonobi ABUJA — Nigeria and the European Union have concluded arrangements for a €20 million defence support package aimed at strengthening the operational capabilities of the Armed Forces, particularly in counterterrorism operations in the Lake Chad Basin. The agreement, the EU’s first bilateral defence support package to Nigeria, is being provided under the European Peace Facility (EPF). The Minister of Defence, Gen. Christopher Gwabin Musa (retd.), disclosed this during a meeting with a delegation from the European External Action Service (EEAS), led by the Head of the European Peace Facility, Claire Gaudin, at the Ministry of Defence Headquarters, Ship House, Abuja. According to a statement issued by the Special Assistant (Media) to the minister, Leah Katung-Babatunde, the meeting focused on finalising arrangements for the delivery of the support package, which was sealed in October 2026. Speaking during the meeting, Musa reaffirmed Nigeria’s commitment to developing indigenous defence capabilities and achieving self-sufficiency in military equipment and technology. He welcomed the EU assistance, describing it as a boost to the operational effectiveness of Nigerian troops engaged in security operations. The minister urged the EU to build on the momentum generated by the recently concluded Africa Defence Exhibition (AFRIDEX) by supporting the establishment of local defence production lines in Nigeria. He also reiterated Nigeria’s determination to track and dismantle terrorist financing networks across the world, irrespective of where they operate. Musa explained that the current phase of the EU support would focus on non-lethal military supplies, including equipment, technical training and maintenance. He expressed optimism that subsequent phases would cover other critical areas, particularly military medical support and advanced surveillance capabilities. Earlier, Gaudin said the €20 million package would provide counter-improvised explosive device (C-IED) equipment, counter-unmanned aircraft systems (C-UAS), night-vision capabilities and personal protective equipment for troops deployed in operational theatres. She said the priority areas were jointly identified and agreed upon with the leadership of the Armed Forces of Nigeria following extensive bilateral consultations. Gaudin added that Nigeria was among more than 20 African countries and 30 beneficiaries globally receiving assistance under the European Peace Facility. She said the package would complement wider regional stabilisation efforts, particularly operations under the Multinational Joint Task Force (MNJTF). The Nigerian and EU delegations also explored opportunities to deepen security cooperation in maritime operations, with particular attention to strengthening security across the Gulf of Guinea. business.title: FutureBit’s Apollo III Bitcoin Miner Hits Micro Center Shelves in Its First Brick-and-Mortar Launch
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine FutureBit’s Apollo III Bitcoin Miner Hits Micro Center Shelves in Its First Brick-and-Mortar Launch FutureBit is putting its Apollo III Full Node on sale Friday at four Micro Center stores, the first time customers can walk into a shop and take home one of the Brooklyn company’s bitcoin miners. The compact home miner, which also runs a full bitcoin node, will be sold in Brooklyn, Miami, Tustin, California, and Austin, Texas, as those stores open Friday, FutureBit said in a release. The four-store launch coincides with the grand opening of Micro Center’s new Austin store, the chain’s 31st U.S. location and its third in Texas. Customers will also be able to reserve a unit online for in-store pickup, the company said. It did not say how many units each store has in stock, or what Micro Center is charging for them. Until now, buyers in North America had to order the machine from FutureBit’s website, where the company says units are in stock and ship in two to three days. Putting it on a computer-store shelf lets a customer look at the hardware, ask how it works and carry it out the same day. “When we started FutureBit, we made weekly trips to the DIY electronics section at the Brooklyn Micro Center to buy parts,” said John Stefanopoulos, founder of FutureBit. “On Friday, someone can walk into that same store, ask how Bitcoin mining works and take home a miner we designed just down the street. We couldn’t be more excited to work with Micro Center on our first physical store launch.” A 6-inch miner that also runs a full node FutureBit’s own shop lists the Apollo III Full Node at $1,099.99 without a storage drive, $1,299.99 with 1 terabyte of SSD storage and $1,399.99 with 2 terabytes. A cheaper, miner-only “Standard” model starts at $899.99 but does not include the full node. The Full Node is rated at up to 18 terahashes per second in Turbo mode, at about 325 watts. In Eco mode, it is listed at about 12 TH/s and 150 watts, with noise under 35 decibels. A Super Eco mode is listed at about 8 TH/s and 80 watts. Power can be adjusted from 50 to 400 watts, and Turbo mode is much louder, at about 55 decibels. Those power figures are measured at the board and can vary by 10%, the product page says. The unit is a 6.5-by-6.5-by-6-inch cube that weighs 6.5 pounds, comes with a one-year limited warranty and is assembled in the United States. It uses new 3-nanometer, American-designed chips, a custom controller and 8 GB of memory, and it includes a built-in solo mining pool. Buyers can also point the miner at a standard bitcoin mining pool. FutureBit says the full node and solo-mining features require an SSD, which is not included in the $1,099.99 configuration. Home mining is not a profit play Bitcoin Magazine covered the Apollo III’s debut in February, when FutureBit introduced the hardware as a way for individuals to run both a miner and a node at home. There is a lot that goes into establishing a successful business. It requires developing the business idea, securing clients, building a customer base and eventually bringing people on board. Starting a business and watching it grow can be an exciting experience. However, one thing many start-up founders overlook is the importance of having the right organisational structure in place. It is one thing to have a great business idea and attract talented employees, but it is another thing to create an environment where everyone understands their responsibilities, knows who they report to and can work effectively towards achieving the company’s objectives. I once worked with a client who needed a new set of employees for a business establishment that was reopening after a period of restructuring. As part of the recruitment process, the first thing I ensured was that a manager was hired before proceeding to fill the remaining vacancies. The idea was simple. The manager would oversee the day-to-day running of the establishment, ensure that company policies were implemented and periodically train employees based on the requirements of their respective roles. During the recruitment process, I clearly communicated each employee’s responsibilities and the person they would be reporting to. These details were also stated in their respective offer letters, so everyone understood their roles and the management structure they were expected to work within. However, there was a challenge. Before the manager was hired, an accountant who was personally known to both co-founders had also been in charge of the previous employees. Following the restructuring, the founders had communicated their desire for a new operational arrangement, and this was clearly reflected in the recruitment brief. Although the new employees understood that they were expected to report to the newly hired manager, the existing employees still had their loyalty to the accountant, who had previously been in charge. entertainment.title: Uwaezu Kanu: Why Motherhood Feels Different for Women in Their 40s Today
entertainment.description: “Oh my God, Uwaezu! You need to hear the latest gist!” My younger sister buzzed with excitement. Though we had been living in different countries for a couple of years, we still made time to talk every single week. Unfortunately, when she called, I couldn’t talk on the phone as I had been ambushed by my kids, who were brandishing their homework and threatening to cry if I didn’t help them. As a mom herself, she immediately understood why I couldn’t continue with the conversation. I quickly made my excuses, and we laughed and hung up, promising to catch up at a more convenient time. However, that exchange got me thinking about how most millennial women have a radically different marriage and motherhood timeline from our mothers. You see, when my mother was in her early 40s, my siblings and I were in university, so she had a lot of free time during the week to spend relaxing, hanging out with her friends, and attending social events. Basically living her best life. I, on the other hand, at 40-plus, spend my days cooking pot after pot of hot meals that immediately get devoured by my ever-hungry kids, teaching my nursery school-aged kids how to count and spell, and trying but often failing to enforce a strict bedtime with yelling and threats. I constantly feel myself going underwater and have to fight for my life every single day. There are other ways motherhood has been such a hugely different experience for me than it was for my mother. Like many women of her generation, she got married right after secondary school as university education was not seen as vital. This meant that she was a teenage mother and so had more energy to spare on her kids. She also benefited from having a lot of support from domestic staff and relatives. I do not have any village supporting me with child-rearing. I have hired domestic staff in the past, but it was always one thing or another, and they ended up leaving me stranded. I also do not have youth on my side, and I have the back pain and other aches to prove it. But this experience is not unique to me. Statistics show that most women globally will have their first child at 30 or 31, and we are seeing a lot more women becoming first-time moms at 35 and above. This is considered advanced maternal age. The fact is that as women increasingly prioritise university education and career stability before marriage, maternal age will continue to rise. This is not a trend that can be reversed. entertainment.title: “Lagos Gave Me My Greatest Successes and Deepest Heartbreak”: DJ Cuppy Opens Up in Ifeoluwa Documentary
entertainment.description: Nigerian DJ and philanthropist Florence Otedola, popularly known as Cuppy, pictured wearing gold headphones and a camel-brown blazer. On her birthday, Florence Ifeoluwa Otedola is giving viewers a more personal glimpse into her life, exploring home, family, identity and purpose. For years, Nigerians have known Florence “Cuppy” Otedola as the internationally recognised DJ and philanthropist, often recognised by her signature pink hair and vibrant public personality. This birthday, however, her new documentary offers a closer look at the woman behind that familiar public image. Released on 11 November 2026, her new 12-minute documentary, Ifeoluwa , follows Cuppy back to Lagos, the city that shaped her and remains close to her heart. It is also a place connected to some of her greatest successes and deepest heartbreak. The title Ifeoluwa means “The Love of God”. Rather than marking the occasion with another glamorous birthday celebration, Cuppy has chosen to share a more reflective portrait of her life. The film explores womanhood, ambition, identity, belonging and the ongoing process of becoming. There are tender moments, too. Viewers see Cuppy not just as a public figure, but as a daughter, sister and granddaughter. Her time with her grandmother offers an especially intimate glimpse into the affection and family ties at the heart of her story. The documentary also captures an evolution audiences may already have noticed. Her signature pink hair has given way to a new look, while faith, education and service have become increasingly central to how Cuppy speaks about her future. This is not a rejection of music, but a fuller picture of the person behind it. Her philanthropic work remains an important part of that picture. Through the Cuppy Foundation, she has helped raise more than $17 million to support displaced children in Nigeria, in partnership with Save the Children. She has also established education funds at the University of Oxford, New York University and King’s College London to help students overcome financial barriers, particularly those from Africa. Alongside this work, Cuppy remains active as an international DJ, with performances at Glastonbury, Wireless Festival and Cannes Lions, as well as events during United Nations General Assembly week. At its heart, Ifeoluwa is a personal homecoming that brings together family, faith, Lagos and the experiences shaping Cuppy’s next chapter. It offers viewers a chance to see beyond the familiar celebrity image and learn more about the person behind it. sports.title: Haslem Sets The Tone For Giannis And Bam After Rough Start
sports.description: Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images The Miami Heat are sitting at 5-6, a record that makes no sense for a team that traded the world to get Giannis Antetokounmpo. The Greek Freak is putting up big numbers, but the losses keep piling up. That kind of pressure usually makes stars question their choices. Instead, Heat legend Udonis Haslem stepped in to set the record straight for his new teammate. This week, Antetokounmpo was addressed directly by Haslem, the vice president of basketball development. The 46-year-old veteran told the star that he cannot pick and choose when the hard times happen. According to HITC , Haslem said: “I told Giannis today: ‘Listen, you don’t get to pick and choose when the adversity hits. You just pick and choose how you respond.'” This message cuts through the noise and tells the team exactly what they need to hear right now. Adversity Hits Early or Late Haslem knows this league better than most, having spent 20 years in a Heat uniform. He explained that bad stretches come for everyone, just at different times. Some teams face trouble at the start, while others get hit in the middle or at the end. The Heat are dealing with it right now, and Haslem sees that as a blessing in disguise. He told Antetokounmpo that getting the pain out of the way early is the better option than saving it for the end of the season. The advice is simple but hard to follow. You cannot change the schedule or the opponents, but you can control your reaction. Haslem noted that if a player gets to choose, they should choose to face the hard stuff now. This approach forces the team to grow faster instead of waiting for a crisis later. Bam Must Play His Own Game While Giannis gets advice on mindset, center Bam Adebayo gets a reality check on his style. Haslem told Adebayo to stop trying to be someone else. The veteran captain made it clear that Adebayo has the talent to score 30 points a night, but he needs to do it his way. According to HITC, Haslem said: “You’re an effort and energy guy, that has All Star talent. You’re not Joel Embiid.” Haslem pointed out that Embiid can score from a kneeling position, but Adebayo’s path to those numbers requires constant motion and intensity. The goal is not to copy a different player’s moves but to use his own unique strengths to dominate. Before retiring, a man who previously shared a locker room with Adebayo made these comments. Haslem has watched Bam grow into a leader and knows exactly what he brings to the floor. The Heat need both stars to buy into these roles to fix their defensive rating, which currently sits as the fifth-worst in the league. The team faces a long road to fix their defense, but the leadership is finally speaking up.

sports.description: France beat South Africa for only the second time in their last 11 Tests dating back to 2009 (FRANCK FIFE) France pulled off a stunning and nervy 21-19 victory over world champions South Africa in the Nations Championship on Friday. A brilliant first-half display and gutsy second-half showing amid a flood of cards handed Les Bleus only their second win over the Springboks in their last 11 Tests. Captain Antoine Dupont was named man of the match in a pulsating encounter that contrasted the running invention of the French with South Africa's bludgeoning force. And in the end, the only difference was a missed conversion by Springboks replacement fly-half Manie Libbok. France, though, were almost undone by wayward kicking, especially from half-back Maxime Lucu. The hosts' backs sparkled in the first half with wings Aaron Grandidier-Nkanang and Louis Bielle-Biarrey, and full-back Theo Attissogbe scoring a try each in a scintillating first half. But South Africa's brute force and forward power kept them in touch, scoring two catch-and-drive tries. Tries from hookers Jan-Hendrik Wessels and Malcolm Marx, and a close-range effort from replacement scrum-half Cobus Reinach, helped them storm back from a 21-7 half-time deficit, but it was not enough. It was South Africa's first defeat in the tournament and hands the initiative to New Zealand in the southern hemisphere pool. France, though, ensured that they will maintain their lead in the northern hemisphere section ahead of next weekend's clash against Argentina, keeping them in pole position to reach the final at Twickenham in two weeks' time. - Electrifying - The build-up to the match had been peppered with mind games. sports.title: Willis On IR: Dolphins Coach Shuts Down Any QB Debate For Now
sports.description: Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images The Miami Dolphins made their move on Tuesday by placing starting quarterback Malik Willis on injured reserve. Placing starting quarterback Malik Willis on injured reserve comes after an MRI on Monday showed his core muscle injury had gotten worse. Coach Jeff Hafley confirmed the team’s stance on Wednesday, stating there will be no quarterback controversy while backup Kyle McCord takes over. The coaching staff wants Willis to rest so he can return healthy, but the immediate path forward belongs to McCord. Hafley explained that he watched Willis struggle to move during the loss to Detroit in Week 9. “You look back at Malik and you watch him in that last game and you could see it,” Hafley said Wednesday, according to WPBF . He noted that Willis was gritting through the pain but could not move like he did earlier in the year. The team signed Willis to a three-year, $67.5 million deal in March, yet his health remains the biggest question mark for the franchise. McCord Takes The Reins Kyle McCord is now the man under center for the upcoming matchup against the Indianapolis Colts. This summer, McCord was obtained by the Dolphins from the Green Bay Packers in exchange for a future sixth-round pick. He has not taken a regular-season snap for Miami yet, but he is ready to compete. “I pride myself on just being the ultimate competitor out there on the field,” McCord said Wednesday, according to Sports Illustrated . He believes his speed in processing information and accuracy will help him succeed in his first NFL start. Hafley was clear that he sees no debate about who starts if Willis does not return soon. “You guys will ask me,” Hafley said, “yes, he’ll be the starting quarterback if he returns.” The coach added that the team needs to get through the next four weeks to see how many games remain in the season. “I think you get through these four weeks, so it would leave four or five games left, and we’ll see,” Hafley said. This timeline will determine if the team can bring Willis back before the season ends. A Tough Road Ahead In his initial eight starts, Willis has thrown six touchdowns and six interceptions while completing 58.2% of passes for 1,396 yards. He showed the arm talent and mobility that brought him to Miami, but his decision-making has been inconsistent. The loss to the Lions on Sunday, Nov. 8, was ugly, with Willis throwing an interception and recording just 128 passing yards. His groin tightness during that game signaled the injury was becoming a major issue. The Dolphins face a difficult stretch without their planned franchise quarterback. They will play the Colts on Sunday, Nov. 15, at 1 p.m. ET at Lucas Oil Stadium.

They have tried to fill gaps with mid-level exceptions, but the results are mixed. Adding a high-volume scorer like LaVine would change the offense. He is averaging 22.3 points per game this season. LaVine Could Fix the Backcourt LaVine is 31 years old and has only four postseason games in his career. He might be looking for a new challenge to boost his resume. According to Heavy.com , NBA insider Jake Fischer reported that Miami is a spot that LaVine would “like to go to.” The Heat cleared their roster to get Giannis, leaving them thin on the wings. They added Klay Thompson and Tim Hardaway Jr., but the depth is still shaky. Among league guards, LaVine previously ranked as one of the top scorers. His numbers have dipped, but his touch remains sharp. He played a career-low 25 games in 2023-24 due to injuries. His scoring ability next to Antetokounmpo would force defenses to choose between two threats. Giannis Is Staying Put While the Heat hunt for new pieces, the future of their star remains uncertain. ESPN front office insider Bobby Marks says Giannis will sign a new deal soon. “Giannis will extend with them either in January or sign a new deal this summer,” Marks said, according to BasketNews.com . He added, “So, it’s not like we’re putting, you know, he’s going to be looking at other things, right?” Giannis is in year two of his fully guaranteed three-year, $175 million max deal. He can choose to keep a player option worth $62.8 million for the 2027-28 campaign. Beginning Jan. 6, a four-year, $275 million extension becomes available for him to sign. If he waits until summer 2027, he could get a five-year deal worth $357 million. The Heat have secured their cornerstone, but the supporting cast needs work. sports.description: Credit: David Kirouac-Imagn Images The Miami Heat cannot afford to lose Davion Mitchell. He has become the engine that keeps this team moving forward. Mitchell is playing as much as much as Bam or Giannis on the team. He has averaged 35.8 minutes per game, which tops the entire roster. His scoring numbers are strong too, with 16.5 points and 8 assists per contest. According to Sports Illustrated , he shoots 49.6 percent from the field and 40.3 percent from three-point range. Those splits are rare and show he does not force bad shots. The Bench Struggles Are Real While Mitchell thrives, Tim Hardaway Jr. is stuck in a deep hole. Hardaway started the season with high hopes but has failed to deliver. He is scoring only 4.3 points per game and shooting under 30 percent from the floor. His defense has been a major problem as well. Coach Erik Spoelstra has had to cut his minutes down to almost nothing. He said, “I get it for Timmy…sometimes you have to make a change.” The team simply cannot play him if he cannot guard or score. Ryan Conwell has taken his spot because he plays with more energy. sports.title: Nikki Hiltz Tells Their Story of Becoming an Olympian After Coming Out as Trans in “Kick”: ‘A Sports Epic’ (Exclusive)
sports.description: Credit: Curren Sheldon NEED TO KNOW Olympic runner Nikki Hiltz tells their story of life as a trans nonbinary athlete in new documentary Kick , alongside fiancée and fellow track and field star Emma Gee “Obviously, it’s not gonna be perfect, but it’s so worth it to try and go for something and let the world surprise you with their support,” Hiltz tells PEOPLE Kick, directed by Julia Schwalb, is available to watch online from Nov. 12 through Nov. 29 Nikki Hiltz doesn’t shy away from telling their story. The Olympian and 11-time national champion, 32, has always been candid about competing in the sport they love as a trans nonbinary athlete. And now, in collaboration with filmmaker Julia Schwalb , Hiltz along with their fiancée and fellow track and field athlete Emma Gee are giving audiences a glimpse into their individual queer journeys and their shared dreams of winning an Olympic medal in the new documentary Kick . Prior to the film’s premiere at DOC NYC on Nov. 11, PEOPLE caught up with Hiltz and Gee, learning how they decided what to share on screen, what they hope audiences take away from the film and how the idea for Kick came to be. “Julia approached me and we got on a Zoom call,” says Hiltz. “One of the first questions she asked was, ‘Okay, if there were to be a film about you, what would you want it to be about?’ And I was like ‘Oh, well, I want a sports movie.’ I’m an athlete and I love a sports epic, you know? That’s sick. I also happen to be queer and nonbinary and that could be part of the film too, obviously, because it’s part of me.’” Nikki Hiltz after winning the women’s mile at the 2026 Prefontaine Classic Credit: Ali Gradischer The pitch for Kick came at the perfect time: when Hiltz was gearing up for the 2024 Olympic Trials, in the hopes of becoming a first-time Olympian. “I was like, ‘Well, I have this big thing coming up. I’m trying to make the Olympics next year. Do you want to film that?’ ” Hiltz says they asked Schwalb. “So it kind of just took off from there.” Three years earlier, Hiltz had hoped to make Team USA for the Tokyo Olympics but finished last in the 1500-meter women’s final, ending their shot. Heading into the 2024 Trials with Hiltz and a camera crew, Gee had some doubts. “There was definitely some apprehension,” she tells PEOPLE. “We had been through the 2021 Olympic Trials together and it was super emotional...During this second Olympic journey, I just wanted to make sure Nikki’s mental health was in a good place — that we were in a safe space to even share this story.” “But we ultimately decided, you know, we’re gonna be on this Olympic journey, whether it’s filmed or not,” she continues. “And I think that it could potentially do a lot of good and offer, you know, representation to not only queer people, but anyone who’s trying to achieve a big goal.” The good news? sports.title: Andorra goalkeeper banned for 12 matches after Jesus de Miguel’s death following on-pitch collision
sports.description: A 12-match ban has been handed to Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono following the death of Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel after an on-field collision between the pair. The Spanish soccer federation’s disciplinary committee imposed the suspension on Friday, 10 days after De Miguel died a day following his clash with Owono. The goalkeeper had received a red card following the incident, and the disciplinary committee said Owono used “excessive force” in the collision. The incident took place near the end of the match in Tenerife on 2 November. De Miguel was chasing a high ball in midfield when he was struck in the chest by Owono, who had rushed far outside his area. The 30-year-old suffered cardiac arrest following the collision. He died the next day. Owono issued a statement through his club expressing his remorse and offering his condolences to De Miguel’s family. Tributes have been paid to Jesus de Miguel following his death (Getty) “These are the most difficult days of my life,” Owono said. “I’m struggling to find the words and finding it very difficult to process anything that has happened. “I feel enormous pain at the loss of Jesus. I think of him, his family, and all the people who loved him. I know there will be many issues to address, and I will face whatever comes with the utmost respect. But right now, honestly, I can’t think of anything other than Jesus and the pain we are experiencing. Rest in peace, Jesus.” Spanish police opened an investigation into possible involuntary manslaughter. Under Spanish law, deaths from non-natural causes, including accidents, are subject to judicial investigation, though prosecutors have said that criminal proceedings are unlikely. On Thursday, Andorra coach Carles Manso said it will be up to Owono to decide when he feels ready to play again. “He is deeply affected by the situation,” Manso said. “We will give him the space to feel completely free to decide whether, and when, he might want to return.” Owono was not selected by Equatorial Guinea for their Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers during the ongoing international break following last week’s collision. Owono has been Equatorial Guinea’s first-choice goalkeeper since he was a teenager and competed with them at the last three Africa Cup of Nations finals.

sports.title: Dolphins Roster Crisis Deepens As Uche Steps Up Amid Injury Woes
sports.description: Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images The Miami Dolphins are facing a brutal stretch with their depth getting tested hard. After losing to the Detroit Lions, the team announced more key starters are sidelined. Head coach Jeff Hafley confirmed that center Aaron Brewer will not play against the Indianapolis Colts. Brewer remains stuck in the NFL’s concussion protocol and has not practiced once this week, per Heavy.com . Rookie wide receiver Chris Bell is also doubtful for Sunday after missing practice with a knee issue. The Dolphins now sit at 1-7 on the season, and their margin for error has vanished completely. Because Malik Willis and Zach Sieler are already on injured reserve, the roster is thin. Sieler suffered a ruptured biceps on the first play of the last game and is out for the entire season. Willis will miss four weeks with a core muscle injury. Now Brewer and Bell add to the list of missing pieces. The team must find a way to win with a backup center and a shaky receiving corps against a struggling Colts squad. Leadership Shifts as Veterans Step In When captains get hurt, someone else has to speak up for the group. Edge rusher Josh Uche has been named a new captain to fill the void left by Willis and Sieler. Uche, a seven-year veteran and Miami native, has been mentoring younger players all season. He accepted the role with a humble attitude, focusing on the upcoming game rather than the honor itself. “It’s still a dream just playing football, man,” Uche said at his locker Wednesday, per the Sun Sentinel . Coach Hafley opened the captaincy to other players who earned the spot, and the team agreed unanimously. Hafley noted that it was good to see players give opportunities to others. Uche plans to keep his head down and do the work needed for the next matchup. “They let me know the news and it’s a plus, but we’re on to the Colts,” Uche said. Lineup Changes and Practice Reports Andrew Meyer is expected to start at center in place of the injured Brewer. Meyer has worked closely with backup quarterback Kyle McCord during practice sessions, which should help their chemistry. Hafley called it a “positive” that the two have already led the scout team together. This familiarity might be the only good news for the offense as they prepare to face the Colts.
